title: Booking an In-Person Hearing Session — Unemployment Insurance Appeals Hearing Office Reference
content:
Under Unemployment Insurance Appeals, a party who asks for an in-person hearing where the docket allows it books the in-person session itself on the calendar of the Department hearing office, and the session replaces the telephone setting on the appeal as a change of hearing mode made at that party's request.

## Not a postponement

A party may ask to postpone a set hearing, and the postponement rules, with their lead time, per-party maximum and reschedule window, govern that request; a party's request to hold its set hearing as an in-person session instead is a change of hearing mode and is not a request to postpone. A change of hearing mode booked as an in-person session is not a postponement: it needs no postponement request or decision, is not subject to the postponement lead time, does not count toward the party's postponements and is not held to the reschedule window; its date is the in-person session date.

## Status of the appeal

An in-person session is not booked on a dismissed appeal until the appeal stands reopened at scheduled status with its reopened hearing date on record.

Put as a condition on the record: while the appeal stands dismissed, no in-person session is booked, and none is booked before the record shows the appeal reopened at scheduled status with its reopened hearing date as the hearing date.

The result governed here is the in-person session date, expressed as the in-person session notice period: the whole number of calendar days from today, the day the party books the session and its notice is mailed, to the in-person session date.

## The tool: `book_in_person_hearing_session_05d44a0a`

**Owner and how it is invoked.** A customer-side tool. The agent unlocks `book_in_person_hearing_session_05d44a0a` and hands it over; the customer themselves — the party who asked for the in-person hearing — runs it to book the session.

**What one call does.** It records a new hearing setting on the appeal in in-person mode at 09:30 local time at the Department hearing office, with its notice mailed today, entered as a change of hearing mode made at the party's request (not a postponement, so no postponement reason is recorded), and it moves the appeal's hearing date to the in-person session date. The party sees the session date on the appeal and in its activity history; the earlier telephone date is no longer the hearing date.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `appeal_id` | the docket number of the party's appeal, as the agent reads it to the party from the appeal record before booking | identifier text |
| `session_days` | the whole number of calendar days from today's date (counted as day 0) to the in-person session date; the figure is given to the party by the agent | an integer; the tool records the session as the YYYY-MM-DD date that many calendar days after today |

**Return.** A text receipt of a dictionary with: `appeal_id` (the docket number), `appeal_event_id` (the reference number of the in-person setting), `hearing_date` (the session date, YYYY-MM-DD), `hearing_time` ("09:30"), `hearing_mode` ("in_person") and `notice_mailed_date` (today's date, YYYY-MM-DD). The call has succeeded when the receipt shows `hearing_mode` in_person and the new hearing date.

*Input and receipt (hypothetical):* booked on 15 April 2026 with `session_days` 23, the receipt shows `hearing_date` "2026-05-08", `hearing_time` "09:30" and `hearing_mode` "in_person".
